text:
oliver.martin: Need help. I moved back to the UK full-time on 2026-04-01 after a 3-year US stint. I updated address in HR but just got a letter from HMRC saying I'm registered for Self Assessment and there's unpaid PAYE for Apr-Jun. I was on US payroll and paid in USD. I thought Redwood would register locally if needed. Help?

zoe.payroll: Sorry you're getting that notice. Short timeline Qs: did you notify payroll of a permanent move and submit any right-to-work docs in UK onboarding? Do you have a UK National Insurance number (NINO)?

oliver.martin: I submitted the move form and uploaded my UK passport + utility bill on 2026-03-28. I do have a NINO. No communication from payroll about PAYE registration.

rishi.tax: Two things to flag: 1) If you're UK tax resident from Apr 1, PAYE should be applied to employment income in the UK. 2) If Redwood kept you on US payroll and didn't apply for a UK PAYE reference, HMRC may expect self-assessment or tax owed. We need to check whether Redwood should have registered an employer PAYE scheme and started RTI reporting.

emma.legal: Also confirm role/location: are you performing duties for UK clients or UK company setup? That affects registration urgency and potential employer liabilities.

oliver.martin: I'm doing product engineering, no UK client contracts, fully remote for UK-based private employer-run product. No contracts signed locally.

zoe.payroll: Action plan: 1) I'll pull your employment status and onboarding docs. 2) We'll check payroll vendor notes to see if UK onboarding ticket was opened. 3) If we missed PAYE registration, our options: register employer PAYE and submit RTI with backdated payroll runs (if vendor allows), or work with HMRC for a payment plan and correct reporting. This can also trigger employer NI and secondary contributions.

rishi.tax: We also need to determine tax residency test details (split-year? automatic overseas test?) If split-year applies, income may be allocated between UK and US periods which affects which pay runs are taxable in UK. That will influence whether HMRC's self-assessment letter is accurate or can be amended.

emma.legal: Please pause any client introductions that could create additional UK presence. Also we should assess permanent establishment risk: if multiple employees work from UK, ensure our legal entity footprint is considered.

zoe.payroll: payroll-bot: logging case.
payroll-bot: Case logged: UK-REG-4858. Assigned to zoe.payroll. Vendor ETA: 48h.

oliver.martin: Thanks. What do I need to do now to avoid HMRC penalties?

rishi.tax: Please upload the HMRC notice to the HR portal and confirm your NINO and date you returned to the UK. We'll use those to liaise with HMRC. Also save payslips and US payroll stubs for Apr-Jun.

zoe.payroll: If we find we failed to register/pay, we will: 1) ask vendor to register PAYE and submit late RTI, 2) calculate employer/employee NICs for the period and either deduct employee NICs via an adjustment or reimburse depending on policy, 3) consider issuing a P60/P45 correction or advise on Self Assessment amendment. This process can take 2-6 weeks.

emma.legal: We'll prepare a short internal memo to document the missed registration and mitigation steps; cc'ing legal counsel for PE exposure analysis.

payroll-bot: Reminder: collect HMRC notice and passport scan.

oliver.martin: Uploaded HMRC letter and my Apr-Jun US paystubs to the portal (link). Thanks for the quick triage.

zoe.payroll: Got them. I'll escalate to vendor + tax counsel now. Expect an update in 48-72h. In the meantime, don't pay HMRC directly until we confirm the right registration path.

oliver.martin: Understood. Appreciate the help.
